builtBy: Extracted from the outbreaks R package 1.9.0 (measles_hagelloch_1861) and rewritten as a point layer. No value was altered; the georeference was added, and is recorded below.

dataset.name: Measles in Hagelloch, Germany, 1861
dataset.collected: Albert Pfeilsticker (1863), Beitrage zur Pathologie der Masern mit besonderer Berucksichtigung der statistischen Verhaltnisse, MD thesis, Eberhard-Karls-Universitat Tubingen
dataset.reanalysed: Heike Oesterle (1992), Statistische Reanalyse einer Masernepidemie 1861 in Hagelloch, MD thesis, Eberhard-Karls-Universitat Tubingen
dataset.distributionChain: Niels Becker (ANU) to Peter J. Neal (Manchester), into the surveillance R package as hagelloch.df, reformatted into outbreaks 1.9.0 by Simon Frost
dataset.licence: NONE STATED by any holder in the chain, checked 2026-10-17 across surveillance, outbreaks and EpiCompare
dataset.licenceDecision: Treated as public domain by the practitioner on 2026-10-17. The 1863 source is out of copyright by age, the records are facts about an 1861 outbreak, and the table has passed openly between studies for thirty years with no holder claiming rights. The structured arrangement is Oesterle's 1992 reanalysis and is not public domain by age, so this is a judgement about copyrightable subject matter and not a licence grant. See docs/research/data-sources.md.

georeference.addedBy: This project, 2026-10-17. NOT PART OF THE SOURCE.
georeference.why: x_loc and y_loc are metres from an arbitrary local origin, not a geographic CRS. Nothing can be mapped without an anchor.

anchor.place: The local origin (x_loc 0, y_loc 0), placed on the 1824 Flurkarte NW III 3 by fitting the case houses to the buildings the sheet draws

georeference.method: Local metres treated as offsets from the anchor, converted at that latitude. Metres per degree from the standard WGS84 series at 48.5403704 N.
georeference.reversible: x_loc and y_loc travel unchanged on every record, so the original frame is recoverable and the anchor can be replaced.
georeference.doesNotEstablish: That any house is where this places it. The source gives RELATIVE positions only; the absolute siting is this project's. It is fitted to the drawn buildings of an 1824 sheet, 37 years before the outbreak, so it is accurate to the street, not proven to the building: 47 of the 56 houses fall on a drawn building and 9 do not. Distances and patterns within the village are the source's; the position on the earth is not.
georeference.corrected: 2026-11-10. The anchor until then, 48.54083 N 9.06056 E, was the English Wikipedia coordinate, which places the village 3.7 km east of where it is, in Tubingen's Waldhauser-Ost (OpenStreetMap places the Berliner Ring there). The German Wikipedia (48 32 27 N, 9 0 43 E), OpenStreetMap (48.5408, 9.0118) and the 1824 Flurkarte NW III 3, placed from its frame, agree on about 9.012 E. The latitude was right and is unchanged; every longitude moved by -0.0486156 degrees, so every distance between cases is as it was. Next: the cases fitted to the houses the 1824 sheet draws (experiment 201).
georeference.fitted: 2026-11-10. The 56 distinct case houses (x_loc, y_loc) were searched over rotation, scale, mirroring and position for the placement that puts most of them on the buildings drawn on Flurkarte NW III 3 (1824, Landesarchiv Baden-Wurttemberg, Public Domain Mark, http://www.landesarchiv-bw.de/plink/?f=2-5311730), the buildings found as dense ink on the scan. Best: north up (rotation 0.0 degrees), scale 1.01, local y to the north; 84% of houses on a building (80% at the coarse step). The same search on 12 random sets of 56 points (6 uniform over the same extent, 6 with x and y shuffled) reached 63% to 68%. The sheet itself was placed from its frame's Gauss-Kruger corners (residuals 0.06 m). The source's metres were kept as they are; only the anchor moved: 151 m west and 51 m south of the 2026-11-10 morning anchor (48.54083 N 9.0119444 E), which had put the origin at the village rather than at its south-west corner.
georeference.corroborated: 2026-11-10. The same search, run against today's OpenStreetMap buildings (674 footprints read by Fieldwork's polygon layer reader from Geofabrik's tuebingen-regbez-261108.osm.pbf, ODbL; not redistributed here), found the houses north up (rotation -0.5 degrees), scale 0.99, centred within 3 m of where the 1824 sheet put them: 89% on a building today, against 63% to 70% for 12 random sets. Placed exactly as the sheet put them, with no search, 42 of 56 fall on a building today. Two independent maps, 200 years apart, agree on the anchor to about the width of a house.

columnsThatBreakAssumptions.date_of_death: Empty for 176 of 188 because those patients RECOVERED. An absence that is an outcome, which this application's quality model reads as a missing value. See experiment 117.
columnsThatBreakAssumptions.complications: A single value, 'yes', on all 188 records. Constant, and therefore carries no information.
columnsThatBreakAssumptions.class: 0, 1, 2 are pre-school, first class and second class. Ordinal, profiled as a quantity with a median.
columnsThatBreakAssumptions.case_ID, family_ID, infector: Identifiers, profiled as quantities. infector is a foreign key into case_ID.

sheet.altered: No: the file as the archive serves it.
sheet.usedFor: Hagelloch's fourth workflow, the 1824 sheet placed by hand: placed by hand from four street junctions (experiment 201); and the anchor fit (georeference.fitted).
